"Act as an expert Mobile Game Developer and Technical Artist specializing in Unity (URP) / Unreal Engine 5 for mid-range Android/iOS devices. 

I want to build an **Offline PvE Tactical Extraction Shooter** for mobile with **realistic graphics** that runs smoothly at 60 FPS on mid-range smartphones (e.g., Snapdragon 7-series / Dimensity 8000-series, 6GB-8GB RAM).

Please provide a comprehensive Game Design @COMMENT_BODY@ Technical Architecture blueprint covering the following:

1. **Core Gameplay Loop (Offline PvE Extraction):**
   - **Pre-Raid (Safehouse/Stash):** Inventory management, weapon modding (attachments), loadout selection, and an offline AI Black Market/Trader system.
   - **In-Raid:** Tactical movement (crouch, prone, lean left/right), realistic ballistics (recoil, bullet drop, armor penetration), looting containers/dead AI, dynamic health system (limb damage, bleeding, painkillers), and timed Extraction Points.
   - **Post-Raid:** Keep loot if extracted; lose uninsured gear if killed in action (KIA).

2. **Realistic Graphics Optimization for Mid-Range Mobile:**
   - Lighting setup: Baked Global Illumination (Lightmaps) combined with Light Probes instead of heavy real-time shadows.
   - Materials @COMMENT_BODY@ Shaders: Using PBR textures with channel packing (ORM: Occlusion, Roughness, Metallic in one texture) and Triplanar/Detail maps to keep texture memory low.
   - Performance techniques: Occlusion Culling, aggressive LOD (Level of Detail) groups, GPU Instancing for foliage/props, and FSR/upscaling techniques.

3. **Smart Offline Enemy AI (Scavs @COMMENT_BODY@ Bosses):**
   - Behavior Tree / State Machine logic: Patrol, investigate gunshot sounds, take cover, flank the player, and suppressive fire.
   - Performance optimization for AI: Distance-based AI throttling (reducing update tick rates for distant bots).

4. **Mobile Tactical Controls @COMMENT_BODY@ UI/UX:**
   - Ergonomic touch controls for complex tactical actions (ADS, lean, reload check, quick-heal wheel, looting interface) without cluttering the screen.

5. **Step-by-Step Starter Code / Project Structure:**
   - Provide the C# (Unity) or C++ (UE5) folder structure and a clean starter script for the **Tactical Weapon @COMMENT_BODY@ Recoil System** or **
Inventory/Loot System**.

เกมได้รัแรงบันดาลใจจากเกท arena breakout mobile

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable offline PvE tactical extraction shooter prototype for mobile, inspired by extraction-shooter conventions.

## Requirements
- Provide a complete safehouse, raid, loot, combat, AI, extraction, HUD, and mobile-control experience.
- Use a realistic visual direction optimized for mid-range mobile hardware.
- Include a technical architecture blueprint with Unity URP structure and starter recoil code.
- Create the game without asking clarifying questions.

## Decisions
- Built an original browser-playable top-down tactical extraction prototype rather than a Unity project.
- Used an industrial “OUTLAND” theme with a restrained military-olive visual style.
- Assumed a 500–700 m compact raid map and offline solo PvE scope.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created the safehouse UI, operator loadout panel, weapon-modification modal, credits, and mission selection.
- Implemented raid gameplay with movement, aiming, shooting, reload, healing, crouching, containers, loot transfer, enemies, health/armor, extraction, minimap, and raid results.
- Added desktop and mobile touch controls.
- Added a tactical map and rail-yard-style industrial environment.
- Created `PROJECT_BLUEPRINT.md` with architecture, gameplay, AI, graphics, UI/UX, Unity folder structure, and starter recoil code.
- Validated `game.js` syntax with `node --check game.js`.
- Started a local HTTP server on port 3000.
- Installed the Playwright Chromium browser for visual verification after its initial missing-browser error.

### Active
- Final browser screenshot verification is pending.

### Blocked
- Browser visual verification was not yet completed; the new browser installation was only just finished.

## Next Move
1. Open `http://localhost:3000` with Playwright.
2. Capture and inspect desktop and mobile screenshots.
3. Verify safehouse deployment, raid rendering, loot, extraction, and responsive layouts.
4. Fix any visual or gameplay defects found during verification.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Main safehouse and raid interface.
- `style.css`: Full responsive visual system and mobile controls.
- `game.js`: Complete prototype gameplay logic and canvas rendering.
- `PROJECT_BLUEPRINT.md`: Unity URP production architecture and implementation guidance.

## Important Context
- The prototype is not an actual Unity/UE5 build; it is a browser implementation using HTML, CSS, Canvas, and JavaScript.
- `game.js` contains the complete gameplay loop, AI, looting, extraction, HUD, desktop input, and touch input.
- The server was started with `python3 -m http.server 3000`.
- Initial Playwright verification failed with: `Browser "chromium" is not installed`.
- Chromium was subsequently installed successfully.
